chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, who said:
The woman, when she prostrates, should be clasped (compact), and the man, when he prostrates, should be open (spread out).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a man's and a woman's posture during prostration in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the normative distinction in prayer postures, where women adopt a compact stance to preserve modesty and conceal their form, while men adopt an open stance to display strength and stability. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is rooted in the principle of *satr* (covering) and reflects the differing physical and social presentations prescribed for each gender during worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions who said,
‘The woman, when she perform Sujūd (plural of Sajdah), should be clasped, and the man when he perform Sujūd, should be open’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain persons of our people who has narrated the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
woman when performing Sajdah (prostration) should not spread herself and man should spread himself on the ground.’”
